Observed lift is large and broad: with-skill passed 41/41 assertions (100%), versus 14/41 (34.1%) without skill, an absolute gain of 27 assertions and 65.9 percentage points. The benchmark's unweighted mean scenario pass-rate delta is reported as +0.64 because scenarios contain different assertion counts.

The lift is not confined to formatting. The strongest discriminators are lifecycle coordination and state integrity: first-create bootstrap plus one accepted history entry; saved-versus-live separation; workspace-owner handoff; root-project/suborganization placement; exact schedule synchronization; deployed-result retrieval; and scoped deletion with recovery.

Important safety discriminators include caps before spend, per-call maxUsd, per-row failure isolation, three-row pilots, explicit-body authenticated HTTP starts, consequential-run gates, secret transfer through the shell, the Gateway-key gate before project linking, cancellation without deployment mutation, ignored runtime data, and scoped persistence. Without the skill, some generic safe behavior remained, but credential safety, gate ordering, persistence discipline, and exact consequence previews were inconsistent.

Lifecycle-specific evidence is especially strong where generic competence was insufficient: without-skill scored 0/5 on local creation, 0/4 on deployed-result inspection, 1/4 on nested ownership, and 1/4 on switching run location. It did better on locally obvious operations such as preserving unrelated deletion artifacts, constructing a cron entry, route-starting a run, and avoiding workspace creation, showing that the skill primarily supplies the cross-step contract and authority model.

Inspection behavior improved from merely reading obvious workflow facts to interpreting managed state correctly: canonical shared files were checked without mutation, missing run data was not mislabeled as a defect, deployment metadata selected remote inspection, authenticated results were fetched safely, and ignored result files were saved without changing tracked state.

The candidate averaged 124.0 seconds and 23,271 normalized tokens per scenario versus 108.9 seconds and 16,812 without the skill. These figures are descriptive because each scenario and configuration has one recorded run.

Evidence limits: all assertions are deterministic and many are compound, so a pass proves the combined observable outcome but cannot isolate which individual instruction caused it. The ten scenarios cover all five lifecycle verbs plus deployment and missing-workspace handoff, but do not establish behavior for every exception, recovery row, triggered workflow, unsafe-URL case, polling timeout, persistence failure, Hobby cron limitation, backend fallback, or custom destination.

The comparison is configuration-level, not a causal ablation of individual lines. Exact wording and structural assertions favor encoded conventions, while security and lifecycle assertions validate substantive behavior. One run per scenario does not support statistical uncertainty estimates; both executor and analyzer used gpt-5.6-sol.
